nvr.off.title: The NVR is switched off
nvr.off.user: An administrator can switch it on and share cameras with you.
nvr.setup.title: Set up the NVR
nvr.setup.intro: The NVR records your network cameras and recognizes people, vehicles and animals, and plates and faces if you like. You only choose here – you never write a configuration file.
nvr.setup.imageHint: When switched on, TitanOS loads about 1.5 GB from the internet once. You then see the progress on the live page; meanwhile you can already add cameras.
nvr.setup.enrichNo: This NAS cannot recognize plates and faces: that needs a processor with AVX2 and at least 4 GB of memory.
nvr.setup.dockerText: The NVR runs in a container that TitanOS manages itself. Docker has to be switched on for that.
nvr.setup.sleepText: The disks of “{volume}” may sleep so far. While the NVR records they stay awake all the time. Use this volume anyway?
nvr.privacy.title: Privacy notice
nvr.privacy.text: Point cameras only at your own property, not at the street or the neighbours. People who are filmed should know about it – for example from a sign. Faces and number plates are personal data: recognize them only where you are allowed to, and keep recordings no longer than needed.
nvr.state.userDown: The NVR is not running right now. Live pictures and recordings come back once it runs.
nvr.state.starting: The NVR is starting … This takes about a minute.
nvr.state.dockerOffHint: The NVR needs Docker. Nothing is recorded while Docker is off.
nvr.state.noVolumeHint: The recordings live there. The NVR stands still until the volume is back or you choose another one.
nvr.state.stopped: The NVR is stopped – nothing is recorded
nvr.state.error: The NVR could not be started
nvr.state.errorHint: Docker refused the start. TitanOS tries again in a minute.
nvr.failover.title: Detection now runs on: {to} (chosen: {from})
nvr.failover.retryHint: “Try again” restarts the NVR and tries the chosen device once more (a gap of about a minute).
nvr.detector.title: Detection runs on
nvr.detector.cpuHint: The CPU is the slowest way: it gets noticeably loaded and detection reacts more slowly.
nvr.detector.coralPluginHint: Install the plugin “Coral USB” so that the NVR can use the Coral stick.
nvr.storage.volumeHint: This volume stays awake while recording.
nvr.storage.capHint: Once the limit is reached the oldest recordings are deleted first. 0 = no limit; then only the days to keep count.
nvr.storage.usedUnknown: The usage is not known yet.
nvr.storage.capCleaning: The limit is reached: TitanOS deletes the oldest recordings until there is room again. Exports stay.
nvr.storage.capExports: The exports alone already need more room than the limit. So TitanOS deletes nothing right now – no recordings either. Delete exports (under Recordings) or raise the limit.
nvr.live.noneAdmin: Add your first camera: TitanOS searches the network for it or you enter its address.
nvr.live.noneUser: No camera is shared with you. An administrator can change that under Users › Cameras.
nvr.live.onlyRecordings: Live pictures are not shared with you, recordings are.
nvr.live.forbidden: This camera is no longer shared with you.
nvr.live.stillHint: Live video is not running here right now; the picture is renewed every two seconds.
nvr.arrange.hint: Grab a camera to move it, drag the bottom right corner to size it. “Done” saves the arrangement for your account.
nvr.arrange.hintPhone: Set the order with the arrows. “Done” saves it for your account.
nvr.arrange.tile: {name}: arrow keys move, Shift + arrow keys size
nvr.view.title: View
nvr.view.hideBar: Hide the bar at the top in full screen
nvr.talk.insecure: Talking needs a secure connection: open TitanOS with https:// – without it the browser does not hand out the microphone.
nvr.talk.denied: The browser did not hand out the microphone. Allow it for this page in the address bar.
nvr.talk.no_microphone: No microphone was found on this device.
nvr.talk.unsupported: This browser cannot talk to the camera.
nvr.talk.failed: The talk connection to the camera failed. Away from home it only works over VPN or Tailscale.
nvr.talk.camera_gone: This camera is gone, or you may no longer see it.
nvr.talk.not_running: Talking does not work right now: the NVR is not running, or two-way sound is not switched on for this camera.
nvr.talk.no_picture: The camera does not answer. Check the camera’s power and network.
nvr.talk.logout: You are logged out. Log in again to talk.
nvr.talk.forbidden: You may no longer watch this camera live, so you cannot talk to it either.
nvr.ptz.title: Pan, tilt and zoom
nvr.ptz.hint: The camera can be moved in the live view.
nvr.ptz.needsOnvif: Moving only works with cameras connected over ONVIF.
nvr.ptz.notFound: The check found no controls on this camera.
nvr.add.title: Add a camera
nvr.add.intro: Search the network for the camera or enter its address, check the connection and choose what it should recognize, record and report.
nvr.add.searchHint: Finds cameras that speak ONVIF. Takes about three seconds; no password is sent.
nvr.add.none: No camera found. Enter its address below by hand.
nvr.camera.kindHint: ONVIF finds the streams itself. With an RTSP address you enter them directly.
nvr.camera.hostHint: IP address or name in the home network, and the ONVIF port (mostly 80 or 8000).
nvr.camera.mainUrlHint: The RTSP address in full resolution; it is recorded.
nvr.camera.subUrlHint: A small stream for detection saves a lot of computing power.
nvr.camera.loginHint: User and password of the camera, not of TitanOS.
nvr.camera.public: Allow an address outside the home network
nvr.camera.publicHint: Switch on only if the camera really is there. Picture and password then travel over the internet.
nvr.camera.name: Name
nvr.camera.nameExists: A camera with this name exists already (upper and lower case do not count). Choose another name.
nvr.camera.checkFirst: Check the connection first: TitanOS then finds the camera's streams.
nvr.camera.enrichMemory: Plates and faces need at least 4 GB of memory.
nvr.camera.enrichAvx: Plates and faces need a processor with AVX2.
nvr.camera.enrichNo: Plates and faces do not work on this NAS.
nvr.probe.title: Check the connection
nvr.probe.hint: Checks address and login and shows which streams the camera delivers.
nvr.probe.unauthorized: The camera refused the user or password.
nvr.probe.locked: The camera locked the account, probably after too many wrong passwords. Wait a few minutes.
nvr.probe.unreachable: No camera answers at this address.
nvr.probe.not_found: The camera does not know this stream. Check the address.
nvr.probe.no_stream: The camera answers but delivers no stream.
nvr.probe.subUsed: Detection uses the small sub stream.
nvr.stream.lowHint: A small picture of the camera. It saves computing power for detection and small live pictures.
nvr.stream.currentHint: To choose other streams, check the connection first.
nvr.stream.detectHint: Which stream detection searches for people, vehicles and animals. High resolution needs much more computing power.
nvr.stream.detectHighHint: High resolution needs much more computing power. If the camera states its picture size when checked, the NAS scales the picture down to at most 1280 pixels wide for it.
nvr.stream.liveHint: Automatic: small live pictures show the low-resolution stream, a large live picture the high-resolution one.
nvr.stream.single: The camera delivers only one stream. It is used for everything.
nvr.stream.keepOpenHint: The live picture appears at once, even while nothing is recorded. For this the camera stays connected to the NAS all the time.
nvr.stream.keepOpenOffHint: The NAS connects to the camera only when it needs a picture. The live picture then takes a moment longer.
nvr.decoder.title: Decode videos
nvr.decoder.hint: Which graphics unit decodes the cameras' videos for detection. “Automatic” uses the iGPU, without one another Intel or AMD graphics unit, else the CPU. An NVIDIA card decodes only if you choose it here. Without a graphics unit the CPU is loaded more.
nvr.decoder.reason.gone: The chosen graphics unit is no longer in the NAS. Until you choose another, the CPU decodes the videos.
nvr.decoder.reason.vm: The chosen graphics unit is assigned to a VM. Until it is back, the CPU decodes the videos.
nvr.decoder.reason.driver: The chosen graphics unit cannot be used right now: its driver is missing or Docker cannot attach it. The CPU decodes the videos.
nvr.detect.title: Recognize
nvr.detect.hint: What this camera should report and mark.
nvr.detect.singleHint: Plates need a vehicle, faces a person to be recognized first.
nvr.record.title: Record
nvr.record.hint.events: Only while the camera recognizes something chosen above.
nvr.record.hint.motion: Whenever something moves in the picture.
nvr.record.hint.continuous: Around the clock. Needs the most room.
nvr.record.hint.off: Live picture and notifications only, no recordings.
nvr.record.retainHint: Older recordings of this camera are deleted.
nvr.record.aroundHint: Seconds recorded before and after an event (60 at most).
nvr.record.aroundEvents: With “On detected objects” only stretches in which a detected object moves are kept, so the seconds before and after are often missing.
nvr.shrink.title: Delete existing recordings?
nvr.shrink.motion: Of the existing recordings only the parts with motion stay; everything else is deleted.
nvr.shrink.events: Of the existing recordings only the parts with detected objects stay; everything else is deleted.
nvr.shrink.days: Recordings older than {days} days are deleted.
nvr.shrink.generic: The change deletes recordings that exist already.
nvr.shrink.when: This happens about a minute after saving and cannot be undone.
nvr.audio.title: Sound
nvr.audio.hint: Records the camera's sound too and lets you listen live. Off by default.
nvr.audio.none: The check found no sound on this camera.
nvr.audio.twoWayHint: Talk to the camera through the microphone in the live view. The camera needs a speaker for that.
nvr.audio.twoWayNeedsSound: Only works with sound switched on.
nvr.notify.recipientsHint: Who gets this camera's messages and how. The accounts that may see this camera can be chosen.
nvr.notify.recipientsNewHint: Who gets this camera's messages and how. For a new camera only administrators can be chosen: users come in once they have the right to the camera (at the account, under "Cameras").
nvr.notify.userNoBell: User – has no bell in TitanOS, only push and e-mail.
nvr.notify.noDevice: Push: the account has no device signed up for notifications.
nvr.notify.devicesOff: Push: the account's devices have camera messages switched off.
nvr.notify.noAddress: E-mail: the account has not entered an e-mail address of its own.
nvr.notify.noMailServer: E-mail: no mail server is set up (Settings › Notifications).
nvr.notify.noNames: Plates and faces: the account gets no messages about them, as it lacks the right "Names and plates" for this camera (at the account, under "Cameras").
nvr.notify.legacy: This camera used to tell every administrator. They are chosen the way the camera told them so far; after saving, the choice here counts.
nvr.notify.legacyEmail: The e-mail used to go to the address of the NAS. Now it goes to each recipient's own address: choose "E-mail" at the accounts for that.
nvr.notify.stale.gone: Gets nothing: the account no longer exists or is locked.
nvr.notify.stale.noRight: Gets nothing: the account may not see this camera.
nvr.notify.homeAssistantHint: Shows the camera in Home Assistant as a device with sensors (over MQTT, group "Cameras"). These are states, not messages; they go on even while the cameras' messages are off.
nvr.notify.agentHint: The AI agent gets this camera's messages too.
nvr.notify.pauseHint: For this long the camera does not report the same kind (a person, say) again.
nvr.notify.windowHint: Report persons, vehicles, animals, plates and faces at certain times only. "Camera not reachable" is always reported.
nvr.notify.daysHint: The time window starts on these days.
nvr.notify.timeHint: In the time zone of the NAS. If "until" is before "from", the window runs across midnight into the next day. Equal times mean the whole day.
nvr.notify.mainOff: The messages of all cameras are switched off (NVR › Settings › Notifications). Until they are on again, this camera reports nothing.
nvr.notify.mainOnHint: On: each camera reports as set for it. Below is who gets what.
nvr.notify.mainOffHint: Off: no camera reports anything – no bell, no push, no e-mail, nothing to the AI agent. Home Assistant still gets the cameras' states.
nvr.notify.overviewLegacyEmail: e-mail to the address of the NAS
nvr.notify.overviewGone: the account no longer exists or is locked
nvr.notify.overviewNoNames: {name} gets no messages about plates and faces (no right "Names and plates")
nvr.cameras.many: The NVR is designed and tested for up to four cameras. More works but can overload weaker hardware.
nvr.cameras.removeText: Nothing more is recorded from this camera. Its recordings and events stay until their retention ends – administrators find them under “Removed cameras” and under Recordings. Exports stay.
nvr.removed.groupHint: They record nothing and have no live picture. Their recordings and events stay until their retention ends or you delete them; only administrators see them.
nvr.removed.untilUnknown: Removed – recordings until their retention ends
nvr.removed.purgeNeedsRunning: Deleting works only while the NVR runs.
nvr.removed.purgeText: All recordings, events and pictures of this camera are deleted now, kept events too. This cannot be undone; the camera then leaves this list.
nvr.removed.purgeRestart: The NVR restarts once afterwards: the other cameras record nothing for about half a minute.
nvr.cameras.removeRights: The shares of this camera for users are dropped.
nvr.events.unavailable: Events are not available on this NAS yet.
nvr.events.seenHint: A dot marks what nobody has looked at yet. “Seen” counts for the whole NVR, not per account.
nvr.events.keptText: yes – event and picture stay; the recording is still deleted after its days
nvr.events.noMedia: This event has neither a clip nor a picture.
nvr.events.deleteText: The event and its snapshot are deleted. The continuous recording of this time stays.
nvr.rec.noneUser: No recordings are shared with you. An administrator can change that under Users › Cameras.
nvr.rec.empty: There are no recordings of “{name}” on this day.
nvr.rec.missing: Recordings are not available on this NAS yet.
nvr.rec.pickHint: Choose a time on the time line.
nvr.rec.unsupported: This browser cannot play the camera’s video format. Download a clip or use another browser.
nvr.rec.playFailed: The recording could not be played.
nvr.rec.nothingAfter: There is no recording after this time on this day.
nvr.rec.nextEventNone: No further event on this day
nvr.export.title: Export a stretch
nvr.export.hint: Saves a stretch of “{name}” as an MP4 file to download. Exports are never deleted automatically.
nvr.export.name: Name
nvr.export.missing: Exports are not available on this NAS yet.
nvr.export.failedHint: The NVR could not make this clip – mostly because nothing was recorded in that period. Delete it and choose a period with a recording.
nvr.export.deleteText: “{name}” is deleted. The recording itself stays as long as it is kept.
nvr.settings.diagnosisHint: Why detection runs or does not run, with the log.
nvr.settings.backupHint: Settings, cameras, camera rights, known plates and the pictures of known faces are part of the daily backup of the stick. Recordings, events and exports are not backed up.
nvr.settings.offText: Then nothing is recorded and nothing recognized any more.
nvr.settings.offKeeps: Settings, cameras and all recordings so far are kept.
nvr.rtsp.title: Offer camera pictures to Home Assistant
nvr.rtsp.hint: Opens port 8554: Home Assistant then fetches the pictures from the NAS instead of from each camera. With a login of its own; off by default.
nvr.rtsp.loginHint: Enter address, user and password in Home Assistant. The last part of the address is the camera's id.
nvr.faces.title: Known faces
nvr.faces.hint: People the NVR should call by name.
nvr.faces.unused: No camera recognizes faces yet. Switch faces on for a camera under “Recognize”.
nvr.faces.missing: Known faces are not available on this NAS yet.
nvr.faces.name: Name of the person
nvr.faces.nameRule: Letters (accented ones too) and digits, plus - and _, at most 40 characters, no spaces.
nvr.faces.nameProblem.space: No spaces – write for example “Grandma_Erna” or “Grandma-Erna”.
nvr.faces.nameProblem.start: The name starts with a letter or a digit.
nvr.faces.nameProblem.train: “train” is taken by the faces not assigned yet. Choose another name.
nvr.faces.pictureHint: A picture has to show exactly one clearly visible face (JPEG, PNG or WebP, 8 MB at most). Several pictures per person improve recognition.
nvr.faces.deletePictureText: The picture of {name} is deleted and no longer counts for recognition.
nvr.faces.deleteText: The person and all their pictures are deleted. The NVR no longer recognizes them.
nvr.plates.title: Known plates
nvr.plates.hint: Plates with a name, such as “Our car”.
nvr.plates.unused: No camera reads plates yet. Switch plates on for a camera under “Recognize”.
nvr.plates.missing: Known plates are not available on this NAS yet.
nvr.plates.name: Name
nvr.plates.patternHint: Separate several plates per name with commas. A star stands for any characters, e.g. MAB12*.
nvr.plates.badPlate: “{plate}” does not work: a plate has 1–64 characters of letters, digits, spaces and -, plus * for any characters.
nvr.plates.seenOld: “–” means: not among the newest 1000 vehicle events, count and time are not known.
nvr.diag.intro: Everything to see without a terminal why detection runs or does not. No passwords appear here.
nvr.diag.stateText.off: The NVR is switched off; there is no container.
nvr.diag.stateText.docker_off: Docker is switched off. The NVR cannot run like this.
nvr.diag.stateText.docker_starting: Docker is switched on but not ready yet.
nvr.diag.stateText.no_volume: The volume for the recordings is not mounted; the container was removed.
nvr.diag.stateText.pulling: The detection software (Frigate) is loading from the internet.
nvr.diag.stateText.starting: The container runs, the detection software does not answer yet.
nvr.diag.stateText.running: The detection software answers, accepted the settings and the detection device works.
nvr.diag.stateText.stopped: Nothing worked. The NVR waits for you and does not record.
nvr.diag.stateText.error: Docker refused something. TitanOS tries again after a minute.
nvr.diag.restartHint: Tries the chosen detection device once more.
nvr.diag.inferenceHint: How long the device needs to analyse one picture. Below 50 ms is good.
nvr.diag.accelHint: The device node through which the container reaches the NPU.
nvr.diag.firmwareNone: The kernel reported nothing about an NPU.
nvr.diag.decodeYes: Video is decoded by the graphics unit.
nvr.diag.decodeNo: Video is decoded on the CPU (no graphics unit found for it).
nvr.diag.enrichYes: Plates and faces are possible on this NAS.
nvr.diag.containerTimes: Started: {started} · ended: {finished} · ends in the last 5 minutes: {ends}
nvr.diag.shmHint: The pictures for detection live here. If it is almost full a sub stream delivers pictures that are too large.
nvr.diag.logFrigate: The last lines of the detection software.
nvr.diag.logContainer: The last lines of the container.
nvr.diag.copyFailed: The browser did not allow copying.
nvr.reason.npu_firmware_old.title: The NPU firmware of the NAS is too old.
nvr.reason.npu_firmware_old.what: The detection software ships a newer NPU driver than the firmware in the TitanOS image understands. The NPU itself is fine.
nvr.reason.npu_firmware_old.todo: Nothing to repair: detection runs on the next device meanwhile. A TitanOS update with newer firmware fixes it; then “Try again”.
nvr.reason.npu_turbo_unsupported.title: The NPU of this processor is not supported by the detection software yet.
nvr.reason.npu_turbo_unsupported.what: A known bug of the built-in Frigate version on Core Ultra 200 processors (Arrow Lake): it asks the NPU for a setting that does not exist there.
nvr.reason.npu_turbo_unsupported.todo: Choose the iGPU under settings or keep “Automatic”. The NPU works with a newer Frigate version in a TitanOS update.
nvr.reason.npu_missing.title: The NPU was not found in the container.
nvr.reason.npu_missing.what: The device node /dev/accel is missing or the detection software sees no NPU through it – mostly the kernel driver or the firmware is missing.
nvr.reason.npu_missing.todo: Look below at “/dev/accel” and “NPU firmware”. If both are missing this NAS has no usable NPU: choose the iGPU.
nvr.reason.coral_missing.title: The Coral stick was not found.
nvr.reason.coral_missing.what: The detection software saw no Coral stick on the USB port.
nvr.reason.coral_missing.todo: Plug the stick directly into the NAS (a USB 3 port if possible, without a hub), check the plugin “Coral USB” and press “Try again”.
nvr.reason.config_invalid.title: The detection software refused the settings.
nvr.reason.config_invalid.what: TitanOS made a configuration from cameras and settings that Frigate does not accept. The detection device is not to blame, so nothing was switched.
nvr.reason.config_invalid.todo: Take back the last change to a camera and press “Try again”. If it stays: “Copy details” and report it as a bug.
nvr.reason.detector_unknown.title: Detection failed for an unknown reason.
nvr.reason.detector_unknown.what: The detection software ended or the detection device does not answer; the error line fits no known cause.
nvr.reason.detector_unknown.todo: Read the line under “Detail” and the log below. “Try again” tries the chosen device once more.
nvr.reason.not_healthy.title: The detection software did not answer after the start.
nvr.reason.not_healthy.what: The container ran but Frigate could not be reached for five minutes.
nvr.reason.not_healthy.todo: Look into the log below and press “Try again”. A very full NAS (memory) can be the reason.
nvr.reason.engine.title: Docker did not start the container.
nvr.reason.engine.what: Docker refused to create or start the container.
nvr.reason.engine.todo: TitanOS tries again every minute. Docker's message is under “Detail”.
nvr.account.mailHint: Cameras send messages to this address when an administrator adds you to a camera as a recipient by e-mail.
nvr.account.mailNoServer: The NAS has no mail server yet. Until an administrator sets one up, no e-mails are sent.
nvr.rights.title: Cameras
nvr.rights.hint: Which cameras of the NVR this account may see. Without a switch it does not see a camera at all.
nvr.rights.namesHint: "Names and plates": names of recognised faces, names of known plates and plates read by this camera – in events, the live picture and messages. Only together with "Recordings"; without the tick they are left out there.
nvr.rights.adminHint: Owner and administrators always see all cameras and recordings.
nvr.rights.noCameras: No camera is set up in the NVR yet.
nvr.search.settings: NVR › Settings (storage, detection device, faces, plates)
nvr.ha.title: Only with a state in Home Assistant
nvr.ha.hint: Messages about events come only while entities in Home Assistant are as you choose here – for example only while the alarm is armed. “Camera offline” always comes. Recording and detection go on regardless.
nvr.ha.unknownHint: If Home Assistant cannot be reached or a state is unknown, the message comes anyway and says so.
nvr.ha.modeHint: Whether all conditions must hold or one is enough.
nvr.ha.ruleHint: Entity and the states in which messages come.
nvr.ha.none: Home Assistant is not connected. Set up the connection under Control panel › Home Assistant.
nvr.ha.loadFailed: The entities of Home Assistant could not be loaded: {error}
nvr.ha.lastState: At least one state stays chosen.
nvr.events.autoplayMuted: The video plays without sound because the browser allows sound only after a tap. Tap the speaker in the video.
nvr.events.fromRecording: The event's clip is not ready yet; the video shows the recording from the event on.
notify.note.ha_unknown: The condition in Home Assistant could not be checked (not reachable or state unknown), so the message comes anyway.
